'''Grace Andrews''' (May 30, 1869 – July 27, 1951) was an American mathematician. She, along with [[Charlotte Angas Scott]], was one of only two women listed in the first edition of ''[[American Men and Women of Science|American Men of Science]]'', which appeared in 1906.<ref>{{cite book|last=Bailey|first=Martha J.|title=American Women in Science:A Biographical Dictionary|year=1994|publisher=ABC-CLIO, Inc.|isbn=0-87436-740-9|url-access=registration|url=https://archive.org/details/americanwomenins00bail_0}}</ref>

== Education ==
Andrews was one of five children of [[Edward Gayer Andrews]], a Methodist Episcopal bishop and school administrator; she was born in [[Brooklyn]], and moved frequently as a child, including stays in Ohio, Iowa, [[Washington, D.C.|Washington DC]], and Europe. She was a student at [[Mount Vernon Seminary and College]], and obtained her undergraduate degree from [[Wellesley College]] in 1890, taking a five-year program at Wellesley that also included music.<ref name=":0" />

She went to [[Columbia University]] for graduate study, earned an A.M. in 1899, and completed a Ph.D. in 1901. Her dissertation was ''The Primitive Double Minimal Surface of the Seventh Class and its Conjugate''.<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=37344}}</ref>

==Career==
She worked as an Assistant Professor of Mathematics for [[Barnard College]] from 1900 to 1902. She then served as accountant to the Treasurer for [[Wesleyan University]] from 1903 to 1926, working from her home in Brooklyn. She was also an executive in various capacities for the New York branch of the [[Woman's Foreign Missionary Society of the Methodist Episcopal Church]].<ref name=":0">{{cite book| first1 = Judy | last1 = Green | author1-link = Judy Green (mathematician) | first2 = Jeanne | last2 = LaDuke | author2-link = Jeanne LaDuke|title=Pioneering women in American mathematics: the pre-1940 PhDs|year=2009|publisher=American Mathematical Society|location=United States|isbn=978-0-8218-4376-5|title-link= Pioneering Women in American Mathematics |at=[https://books.google.com/books?id=jUrq3bUvQlYC&pg=PA126 pp. 126–127]}} Biography on p.27-268 of the [https://www.ams.org/bookpages/hmath-34-PioneeringWomen.pdf Supplementary Material] at [https://www.ams.org/publications/authors/books/postpub/hmath-34 AMS]</ref>
